analysis: Both units are head-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1617-2394). The only changed range inside them is 1740-1759, which describes behavior already in code. Native-tracked engines (GLM5-Next, MiMo V2.6) refuse token constraints and unqualified topLogprobs rows at submit. `EngineV2Bridge.nativeOutputControlRefusal` maps such requests to a content-free 400 `invalid_request`, so they do not strike the coordinator's inference-error breaker. A GLM5-Next logprob row decodes target-only, with no draft or verify. This prose adds no new attack surface. It narrows the availability risk from caller-triggered 500s (T-010 class). It touches no key custody, attestation, encryption or prefix-cache controls, and the surrounding unchanged text on cache, MTP and media does not contradict the T-041 posture. Its claims about the prefix cache stay within the existing encrypted SSD, HMAC-tag and account-scoped model. Outside my units, the patch excerpt shows a docs change for GLM5-Next. The verified manifest aggregate is published as the weight hash, and the next coordinator-mode start registers it without re-reading the weights while each file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime are unchanged (`VerifiedWeightHashStore`, `ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash`). The text says the load verifies again before serving. If that is right, it is a design change touching T-012 (operator weight replacement) and T-027. It affects the coordinator's weight-hash check, so it is a question for integration or code-level review, not a finding from these units. I could not verify from the supplied text whether stat-identity caching is sound against a root operator, or whether the load-time re-verification really occurs. Findings are empty because the in-scope doc lines show no concrete regression.
